newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: No agreement on SAfrica '97 maize marketing scheme.
newsitem.headline: No agreement on SAfrica '97 maize marketing scheme.

text.p: South Africa's maize industry was unable to reach agreement on the details for a new marketing system for the 1997/98 season on Friday.

The Maize Advisory Committee (MAC) said it emerged at a meeting in Pretoria that processors, traders and other buyers of maize felt there should be no price floor mechanism from the beginning of the new season in May.
However, producers and co-operatives felt some interim safety net was essential, the MAC said in a statement.

It said the different viewpoints would be reported to the Minister of Agriculture who would be requested to make a "directional decision". This would be followed by another meeting of the MAC to discuss future developments.
A proposal to amend the current maize marketing scheme to make provision that no further export pools be opened by the state-owned Maize Board after February 1997 was tabled.
South Africa's domestic maize market was deregulated in 1995 but the Maize Board is still active in the export market where it sets a floor price. --Johannesburg newsroom 27 11 482 1003
